family_history: Maternal grandmother: type 2 diabetes with diabetic foot complications ('Charcot foot'). Father: hypertension. No known hereditary neuropathy.

social_history.note: Senior pharmaceutical sales director. Frequent business travel. Married, one child. Non-smoker. Social alcohol (3-4 drinks per week on average). No illicit drugs. No occupational chemical exposures confirmed by occupational health review.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Normal cognition.
neurological_exam.motor: Right wrist extensors 1/5 (wrist drop — radial nerve territory). Right finger extensors 2/5. Right brachioradialis 2/5. Right biceps 5/5. Right deltoid 5/5. Left hand intrinsics 4/5, left ring/little finger flexion 4/5. Bilateral foot dorsiflexion 4/5, plantar flexion 4+/5.
neurological_exam.sensory: Right radial dorsum of hand — severely reduced light touch and pinprick (radial sensory territory). Left ring and little finger — reduced light touch and pinprick (ulnar territory). Bilateral feet — reduced light touch in stocking distribution to mid-ankle.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally. Triceps 2+ bilaterally. Brachioradialis: absent right (radial nerve lesion), 1+ left. Patellar 1+ bilaterally. Achilles trace right, absent left.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact bilaterally. Gait with mild steppage bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Mild bilateral steppage, greater right than left. Tandem walking impaired.
neurological_exam.special_tests: Right wrist drop confirmed — radial nerve territory. Left ulnar territory sensory loss. No Babinski. Positive Tinel's at right spiral groove of humerus? — equivocal.

patient.chief_complaint: Bilateral foot numbness and weakness for 14 months with recent right wrist drop
patient.history_present_illness: Thomas Gu is a 49-year-old sales director presenting to neurology after developing progressive bilateral foot numbness over 14 months followed by recent onset right wrist drop noted upon awakening 3 weeks ago. He initially attributed his foot symptoms to long hours standing during business travel and tight footwear. His primary care physician obtained EMG 3 months ago which reportedly showed mild sensory neuropathy and attributed it to borderline prediabetes (HbA1c 5.9%). However, the acute onset of right wrist drop was alarming, and the patient was referred urgently. He reports left hand numbness as well (ring and little finger distribution). He has been evaluated for occupational exposures: he works in pharmaceutical sales and denies any chemical exposures. He has noted a 6 kg unintentional weight loss over the past year which he initially attributed to stress and dietary changes. He has also noted intermittent abdominal fullness and early satiety for 6 months. He is a non-smoker and drinks socially but not heavily. He has never used intravenous drugs. He has a maternal grandmother who had 'Charcot foot' from diabetes, and he was therefore not concerned initially. His right wrist drop is now impacting his ability to drive and write, prompting this urgent referral.

Neuropathy and Inflammatory Workup.value: Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia — no M-spike; gamma fraction 28% (elevated)

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL (H), MCV 76 fL (H), Platelets 484 K/uL (H), Eosinophils 980 cells/uL (H), Total Protein 8.8 g/dL (H), Albumin 3.2 g/dL (H), LDH 386 U/L (H), HbA1c 5.9 % (H), ESR 88 mm/hr (H), CRP 28.4 mg/L (H), ANCA (MPO/PR3) ANCA-MPO positive, titer 1:160 (H), SPEP Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia — no M-spike; gamma fraction 28% (elevated) (H), Fecal occult blood POSITIVE (H), Ferritin 4 ng/mL (H), Iron 28 ug/dL (H), TIBC 488 ug/dL (H).

specialized_test.impression: ABNORMAL NCS/EMG — mononeuritis multiplex pattern. Axonal injury involving multiple separate nerves: right radial (severe amplitude reduction with acute denervation on EMG), left ulnar (moderate amplitude reduction, subacute changes), bilateral peroneal (moderate-to-severe amplitude reduction, chronic reinnervation). Amplitude-predominant loss without conduction block. Pattern localizes to multiple individual peripheral nerves in separate anatomic territories, following a stepwise asymmetric course

output.impression: Epineurial necrotizing vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis of medium-sized vessel wall. Transmural eosinophilic and neutrophilic infiltrate. Axonal degeneration in multiple fascicles. Findings of a necrotising vasculitic process; the prominent eosinophilic component on this specimen warrants clinical and serologic correlation.

CT CHEST: Bilateral ground-glass opacities in both lower lobes consistent with eosinophilic lung disease (eosinophilic pneumonia pattern). Small bilateral pleural effusions. No nodules, no cavitation. CT ABDOMEN/PELVIS: Circumferential wall thickening of distal ileum and cecum — eosinophilic gastroenteritis pattern. Mild mesenteric lymphadenopathy. No mass lesion. Bilateral lower lobe eosinophilic pneumonia pattern and eosinophilic gastroenteritis pattern identified

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: BAL Differential — Eosinophils 42% (H), BAL Macrophages 38% (H), BAL Neutrophils 18% (H), BAL Lymphocytes 2% (H).

output.impression: Echocardiogram: LVEF 60% (normal). Mildly increased pericardial effusion (8 mm, trivial-small). No wall motion abnormalities. No valvular abnormalities. No evidence of eosinophilic endocarditis. Small pericardial effusion identified. No evidence of constrictive physiology

Colonoscopy: patchy erythema and mucosal edema from cecum through distal ileum. Biopsies show eosinophilic infiltrate (>50 eosinophils per high-power field) in ileum and cecum — consistent with eosinophilic gastroenteritis. No polyps. No malignancy. No IBD features.

output.interpretation: ANCA-MPO titer decreased to 1:40 (from 1:160) but remains positive. ESR 28 mm/hr (mildly elevated). Hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL (mildly low). Eosinophil count normalized to 180 cells/uL.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA / Churg-Strauss) with vasculitic mononeuritis multiplex

differential.key_features: Same mononeuritis multiplex; differentiate by ANCA pattern (p-ANCA/MPO vs c-ANCA/PR3), eosinophilia, and organ involvement.

differential.diagnosis: Hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies (HNPP)
differential.key_features: Recurrent painless mononeuropathies at compression sites; PMP22 deletion; pain and systemic features here favor vasculitis.
Pure motor, with conduction block; sensory features here exclude MMN.
Mild prediabetes does not cause asymmetric multifocal mononeuritis multiplex.
Similar phenotype; need cryoglobulins, hepatitis C serology, complement.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Vasculitis + paraneoplastic panel (ANA, ANCA, ESR/CRP, RF, complement, anti-Hu/CV2/PNMA, cryoglobulins)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify vasculitic or paraneoplastic etiology in asymmetric/mononeuritis-multiplex pattern

optimal_actions.action: Sural nerve biopsy when vasculitic / mononeuritis multiplex / amyloid suspected
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Necrotizing vasculitis or amyloid deposition or demyelination/onion-bulbs (CIDP) on histopathology

optimal_actions.action: Eosinophil count, IgE, asthma/sinusitis review, and chest imaging for EGPA workup
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Peripheral eosinophilia (>10%), elevated IgE, asthma history support EGPA

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.
EMG/NCS localizes and characterizes lesion before nerve biopsy, guiding which nerve to biopsy and aiding interpretation.

critical_actions: Recognize mononeuritis multiplex with asymmetric motor + sensory loss in named-nerve territories
Obtain ANCA (p-ANCA/MPO vs c-ANCA/PR3), eosinophil count, IgE, ESR/CRP, complement
Sural / superficial peroneal nerve biopsy for necrotizing eosinophilic vasculitis
Initiate high-dose corticosteroids ± cyclophosphamide or mepolizumab after biopsy confirmation
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute to prediabetic neuropathy — symmetric distal axonal pattern is not seen here
Do not delay immunosuppression once vasculitic neuropathy is biopsy-proven
key_reasoning_points: Asymmetric multifocal motor + sensory deficits = mononeuritis multiplex
Asthma / sinusitis + eosinophilia + ANCA (often p-ANCA/MPO) define EGPA
Nerve biopsy of an affected superficial peroneal or sural nerve confirms eosinophilic vasculitis

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Prediabetes does not cause mononeuritis multiplex.
